title: Hot ChipsKeynote
problem: Keynote presentation; no specific technical problem addressed.
method: Keynote address covering emerging trends and research opportunities.

title: 20.6 Fully Integrated Self-Propelling Microrobot in 180nm CMOS with Sub-GHz Parity-Time-Symmetry On-Chip Energy Harvesting and Traveling Wave Electroosmosis Actuation
problem: Autonomous motion integration remains challenging on CMOS dies—prior designs integrate energy harvesting and control, but either rely on lossy magnetic resonance coupling or require specialized photovoltaic fabrication processes incompatible with standard CMOS.
method: This design integrates parity-time-symmetry energy harvesting operating at sub-GHz frequencies with traveling-wave electroosmosis actuation mechanisms on a single CMOS die. The approach uses on-chip electroosmotic channels to generate propulsion forces directly from the harvested energy, eliminating the need for external actuation components or highly sensitive power coupling schemes.

title: UPP: Universal Predicate Pushdown to Smart Storage
problem: Existing in-storage processing (ISP) solutions only support simple operators (equality, range comparisons) on fixed-length columns, leaving modern analytical queries that use complex operators and diverse data formats unaccelerated. There is no flexible ISP mechanism that can handle arbitrary filter predicates used in production databases.
method: UPP defines a compact, purpose-built ISA for predicate pushdown that is separate from individual operator implementations. The database software layer recognizes filter predicates, compiles them to UPP-compliant instructions, and ships them to an FPGA (SmartSSD) where bitwise comparison execution leverages lightweight metadata to evaluate predicates directly in storage without reformatting data. The hardware/software co-design avoids changing input data formats on disk while enabling flexible predicate evaluation through this instruction-level abstraction.

title: Fast End-to-End Simulation and Exploration of Many-RISCV-Core Baseband Transceivers for Software-Defined Radio-Access Networks
problem: Designing high-performance many-core SDR processors for baseband processing requires functional validation and end-to-end performance analysis within realistic wireless environments, but RTL simulation is prohibitively slow.
method: Fast simulation framework using static binary translation with approximate timing model of many-core hardware (1024 RISC-V cores), coupled to wireless channel models. Simulates critical physical layer 5G OFDM detection functions. Single-threaded: 9.5s-3min per symbol (3 OOM faster than RTL); parallelizable to 128 threads with 73-121x speedup.

title: Slim-Llama: A 4.69mW Large-Language-Model Processor with Binary/Ternary Weights for Billion-Parameter Llama Model
problem: LLM ASICs achieve low energy for small models (336-708M parameters) but cannot scale to billion-parameter models due to excessive external memory access (EMA) energy, requiring 26-222pJ/param.
method: Slim-Llama adopts binary or ternary weight quantization with new hardware optimizations for token processing, achieving 9pJ/param energy consumption and sub-5mW power for billion-parameter Llama inference.

title: Clo-HDnn: Continual On-Device Learning Accelerator with Hyperdimensional Computing via Progressive Search
problem: On-device continual learning requires efficient gradient-free training for edge devices with strict power and memory constraints.
method: Clo-HDnn integrates hyperdimensional computing (HDC) with low-cost Kronecker encoding and weight clustering feature extraction (WCFE); progressive search reduces query complexity by 61% by encoding/comparing only partial query hypervectors in a gradient-free learning paradigm.

title: BBAL: A Bidirectional Block Floating Point-Based Quantisation Accelerator for Large Language Models
problem: LLM deployment on edge devices faces memory and computational constraints; Block Floating Point (BFP) quantization loses small and moderate values because all data align to maximum exponent, degrading LLM accuracy.
method: BBAL introduces Bidirectional Block Floating Point (BBFP) format that reduces selection of the maximum as shared exponent, lowering quantization error. Full-stack implementation includes BBFP processing element array and cost-effective nonlinear computation unit, enabling accurate low-bit LLM inference on edge accelerators.

title: DRAFT: Decoupling Backpropagation from Pre-trained Backbone for Efficient Transformer Fine-Tuning on Edge
problem: Efficient fine-tuning of pre-trained Transformers on resource-constrained edge devices, where backpropagation through massive backbone weights incurs high computational cost and memory overhead.
method: DRAFT framework decouples backpropagation via Feedback Decoupling Approximation (FDA) into two pathways: trainable adapter pathway and sparse ternary Bypass Network (BPN). A reconfigurable DRAFT accelerator features lightweight sparse gather networks and dynamic workflows to exploit sparsity and data parallelism inherent to FDA.

title: PhasePrint: Exposing Cloud FPGA Fingerprints by Inducing Timing Faults at Runtime
problem: Cloud FPGA vendors prevent tenants from localizing (identifying) specific FPGA instances to thwart attacks exploiting data remanence and analog covert channels. This paper addresses how to fingerprint and locate individual FPGAs in a shared cloud environment despite vendor-imposed restrictions on low-level hardware information.
method: PhasePrint induces controlled timing faults at runtime by deliberately stressing the FPGA fabric (e.g., via ring oscillators or voltage/frequency manipulation) to elicit device-specific phase signatures in timing behavior. These signatures arise from process-variation-induced differences in propagation delays across FPGA instances. The resulting fault patterns are collected and used as a fingerprint to distinguish one physical FPGA from another without requiring privileged low-level access.

title: 8.4 A 4GHz, 0.69%-Accuracy Voltage-Droop Detector with Multiple Remote Sensing and Under 2-Cycle Detection Latency in 2nm GAAFET
problem: Voltage droop detection in modern SoCs requires both PVT-tolerant direct sensing and remote-capable distributed detection; previous digital detectors (TDC-based) suffer from PVT sensitivity and low conversion gain; analog detectors have bulky blocks, limited integration, and routing/frequency constraints.
method: 2nm GAAFET droop detector with compact distributed remote droop detectors (RDD) sampling at up to 4GHz, synchronized by a PVT-tolerant main droop detection controller (DDC), achieving <2-cycle latency with 0.69% accuracy.

title: INSTA: An Ultra-Fast, Differentiable, Statistical Static Timing Analysis Engine for Industrial Physical Design Applications
problem: GPU-accelerated STA (static timing analysis) fails to gain adoption because it cannot emulate proprietary delay models of commercial tools; high-accuracy incremental timing for iterative design loops is slow.
method: GPU-STA initialized from reference commercial tool (one-time setup), then fine-tuned to model tool's delay characteristics. Differentiable engine enables gradient computation for timing optimization; demonstrated on gate sizing and placement tasks with 25x faster incremental updates.

title: Reinforcement Learning-Driven Window Selection for Enhanced Window-Based Rip-up and Reroute in Chip Detailed Routing
problem: Window-based rip-up and reroute in detailed routing is the most runtime-intensive step due to inefficient window selection that targets violations uniformly, wasting effort on low-congestion areas while missing high-congestion routing hotspots.
method: A reinforcement learning approach dynamically generates windows by adjusting size and position based on design rule violation (DRV) distribution, targeting high-congestion areas efficiently. RL learns predictive window placement that minimizes DRVs, achieving high-quality routing results with competitive runtime.

title: MetaSapiens: Real-Time Neural Rendering with Efficiency-Aware Pruning and Accelerated Foveated Rendering
problem: Point-Based Neural Rendering (PBNR), particularly 3D Gaussian Splatting, is computationally too expensive to run in real time on mobile devices due to the large number of Gaussian primitives and the full-resolution rendering required.
method: MetaSapiens combines two techniques: (1) efficiency-aware pruning that reduces the number of Gaussian primitives based on their contribution to rendering quality, using a pruning criterion that accounts for both visual importance and computational cost on the target hardware; and (2) accelerated foveated rendering that exploits the human visual system's reduced acuity in peripheral regions by rendering the foveal region at full quality and peripheral regions at lower resolution or with fewer Gaussians, reducing total computation. Both techniques are co-designed with the mobile hardware execution model to maximize throughput.

title: Profile-Guided Temporal Prefetching
problem: Temporal prefetching for irregular memory access patterns (data-dependent structures, pointer-chasing) requires metadata to record and replay past access sequences; existing on-chip metadata storage schemes for temporal prefetchers have limited capacity, and prior software-guided approaches have failed to optimize metadata storage management effectively, leaving temporal prefetching 0.1% over baseline with profile-guided methods.
method: Prophet is a hardware-software co-designed framework that uses profile-guided methods to optimize on-chip metadata storage management for temporal prefetchers. Instead of tracing full access sequences, Prophet profiles programs using lightweight hardware counters, then injects hints (compiler annotations) into the program binary to guide the hardware temporal prefetcher's metadata storage management at runtime. Dynamic tuning of these hints allows the optimized binary to adapt to different program inputs without re-profiling. Prophet is designed to coexist with existing hardware temporal prefetchers: it provides optimized metadata management for frequently executed hot paths while the original hardware-only scheme handles less frequent paths.

title: 5.6 A Power-Efficient CORDIC-Less Digital Polar Transmitter Using 1b DSM-Based PA Supporting 256-QAM
problem: Digital polar transmitters require CORDIC for I/Q-to-polar conversion but CORDIC's nonlinearity causes bandwidth expansion of AM/PM outputs, challenging wideband implementations. Switched-capacitor PAs suffer low efficiency at power backoff; existing AM/PM modulation methods (PI, DTC, VMD SCPA) introduce further nonlinearity requiring complex DPD.
method: CORDIC-less digital polar transmitter using intrinsically linear 1-bit PA directly supporting polar AM/PM. Edge-selection-based phase modulation replaces CORDIC. 1-bit DSM-based PA inherently avoids switch-capacitor losses and maintains linearity without digital pre-distortion.

title: FineRR-ZNS: Enabling Fine-Granularity Read Refreshing for ZNS SSDs
problem: Zoned namespace SSDs lack read refreshing mechanisms to guarantee data reliability, and zone-level read refreshing incurs severe overhead due to large valid data movements, degrading I/O performance.
method: Proposes host-controlled fine-granularity read refreshing via metadata remapping at block level, includes zone reconstruction method to retrieve remapped data forming complete data, keeps remapped data available and prioritized for read access until next refresh cycle.
